name: contact_sheet
description: Tile a project's frames into one image, each labelled with its time. Answers look's issues too, the closing check (not for --raw or --frames-dir). With neither --at nor --every it samples every ceil(duration / 60) seconds (at least 1 s, so at most 60 tiles). --every covers the whole project on a grid; --at lists exact times (repeatable), e.g. 12 frame times for a strip. A small --tile-width (360) gives a phone-size view.

output.description: {path, times, cols, tile_width, sheets?: [paths: past 12 frames, 12 or fewer a sheet in 4 columns], sheet_times?, frames?: [abs paths in time order, with frames-dir], look?}

params.name: project
params.description: The project id, its folder, or the absolute path of its project.json

params.name: at
params.description: Sample time in seconds (repeatable; more than 120 are thinned evenly to 120, with a note)

params.name: every
params.description: Sample every N seconds across the project (must be > 0; not combined with --at; one that would pass 120 samples is coarsened to fit, and the answer carries a note)

params.name: raw
params.description: Tile the untouched SOURCE frame under each time instead of the composite: no crop, zoom, fit, grade, image items, overlays or captions. Use it to read the footage itself without making a stripped copy of the project. A time with no video is black.

params.name: frames-dir
params.description: Keep the sampled frame PNGs here (f_0000.png...) instead of discarding them, and report their paths
